list.fact: MBPP (974 basic problems): same story
EvalPlus / HumanEval+ hardened the test suites (80x more tests) and knocked several points off inflated scores

LiveCodeBench: any model can be evaluated on post-cutoff problems only, contamination control by construction

list.fact: SWE-bench (2023, Princeton): 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repos
SWE-bench: repo at the pre-fix commit plus issue text, model must produce a patch, scored by the repo's own fail-to-pass tests

list.fact: SWE-bench turned code evals from function completion into repo-level engineering; de facto coding-agent benchmark

list.fact: Lite (300): cheaper subset, popular 2024, now rarely reported
Verified (500, 2024): OpenAI paid engineers to filter broken tasks (underspecified issues, unfair tests; ~33% of the original had problems)
checks: more than two thirds were filtered out

list.fact: Verified known issues: solution leakage in issue comments, weak test suites, repo-memorization (worse on repos created after cutoff, per SWE-bench-Illusion and SWE-rebench)
Pro (2025, Scale): 1,865 tasks from 41 repos
Pro: copyleft-licensed and private commercial repos as a contamination guard; human-augmented problem statements; multi-file reference fixes
Pro: public-split SOTA ~59% (Scale harness), vendor-scaffold ~80%, private commercial split ~47%; scaffold and split swing a SOTA claim by 30 points
list.correction: the 47% was Opus 4.6 on V1 commercial; versions spliced

list.fact: Multimodal (2024): JavaScript repos with screenshots/visual bug reports
SWE-rebench / SWE-bench-Live: continuously mined fresh issues, monthly updates, decontaminated by recency; cited as the honest alternative
Real-SWE (2026, Specific Labs): ten tasks licensed from real companies' production repositories, median 11 files changed per task
Real-SWE: each model in its native harness over 640 scored rollouts
list.correction: 640 rollouts = 10 tasks x 8 models x 8 runs (108 + 532 in the page's split)
